meaning.because: The owner's own words: phone orders are taken while serving at the counter, and that is when mistakes happen.
meaning.decision: Two goals: at least 15 of the 20 or so cake orders a week come through the website, and the calls just asking when the bakery is open and where it is are cut by half, both within six months of going live. Showing what the bakery bakes serves the first: people choose their cake before they order.
meaning.instead: No goal was turned down; none had been proposed.

meaning.because: The owner asked for the smallest answer; it needs no collected or cancelled status and no extra screen, and it holds nothing for longer than the cake needs.
meaning.decision: An order leaves the list and is deleted the day after its pick-up day, collected or not. A customer who rings to cancel is dealt with by phone, and the staff simply do not make the cake.
meaning.instead: Collected and cancelled statuses, and keeping past orders.

meaning.because: The owner chose this direction when asked about the look.
meaning.decision: Warm kitchen: cosy and handmade, like walking into the shop. No design system and no brand: the name set as a wordmark. It must never look corporate, cold or like a supermarket. It feels warm, handmade and welcoming, for local families and neighbours ordering a birthday cake. Light only: a cream background, crust brown for text and structure, a raspberry accent, a soft green for success and a deep red for errors. A friendly serif for headings and a clean sans for text, both free under the SIL Open Font License with no reserved name. Roomy, with rounded corners and soft shadows. Drawn illustrations of the bakes as inline SVG, and no photos. Phone first, desktop too, text contrast of at least 4.5:1, with visible keyboard focus.
meaning.instead: Fresh and light: white, sage and grey with one sans. Old-town craft: deep green, cream and gold with a classic serif.

meaning.decision: Cakes are ordered for pick-up at the bakery. Nothing is delivered, and only cakes can be ordered on the website.
meaning.instead: Delivery, and ordering other things on the website.

meaning.decision: Customers pay at pick-up. The website takes no payment.
meaning.instead: Paying part or all of it when ordering, which would need a card provider and a payment step.

meaning.decision: Three cakes can be ordered: Victoria sponge 28, Chocolate fudge cake 32, Carrot cake 30. Also baked: Sourdough loaf 4.50, Seeded rye 5.00, Butter croissant 2.20, Cinnamon bun 2.80, Lemon tart 3.50. All in euros. N1 holds the list.
meaning.instead: Nothing else was put forward: the owner named what the bakery bakes.

meaning.decision: To make a cake the bakery needs its size, small serves 8 and large serves 14 and costs 10 euros more, the words on it, up to 30 characters and optional, and any allergies.
meaning.instead: Nothing else was put forward: the owner named what a cake needs.

meaning.decision: Two days' notice for every cake.
meaning.instead: Nothing else was put forward: the owner set the notice.

meaning.because: The owner's answer. Only pick-up days when the shop is open can be chosen.
meaning.decision: Closed Monday. Tuesday to Friday 7:30 to 17:30, Saturday 8:00 to 15:00, Sunday 9:00 to 13:00. 12 Mill Lane, Little Harbury. 01632 960123. N3 holds them.
meaning.instead: Nothing else was put forward: the owner gave the hours and the address.

meaning.decision: The customer is not told. They come on the day they chose.
meaning.instead: Telling them by email or by text.

meaning.because: The target is half of a number nobody has counted.
meaning.decision: The owner counts the calls with a tally sheet for two weeks before go-live.
meaning.instead: Nothing else was put forward: the owner chose the tally sheet.

meaning.name: Look around
meaning.purpose: A customer sees what the bakery bakes and finds a cake they would like.
meaning.steps: 1. The customer opens the home page and sees the three cakes. SC1, R1 2. They open What we bake and read the whole list, with its prices. SC2, R1 3. A cake they like offers Order this cake, and they go on to order it. SC2, R3 4. Anything that is not a cake is only shown. SC2, R1

meaning.goes wrong: The order cannot be recorded: the customer is told it was not placed, with the phone number, and can send it again with nothing lost. SC3, R3
meaning.name: Order a cake
meaning.purpose: A customer ends with a cake ordered for pick-up, its number on the screen.
meaning.steps: 1. The customer chooses Order this cake on What we bake, which brings the cake with it, or Order a cake in the menu. SC2, SC3, R3 2. They enter the cake, its size, the pick-up day, their name and phone number, with the words and any allergies if they want, and select Place order. SC3, R3 3. A detail missing or not accepted is refused beside it, with what they entered kept. SC3, R4 4. A day the bakery cannot do is refused under the day. SC3, R5 5. The order is recorded, and Order placed shows its number, the cake, the day, the price and where to collect it. SC4, R6 6. They collect the cake and pay at the bakery on the day they chose, outside the website.

meaning.name: Find the bakery
meaning.purpose: A customer finds when the bakery is open and where it is, without ringing.
meaning.steps: 1. From any screen, the customer reads the opening hours, address and phone number in its foot. SC1, R8 2. Or they select Find us and read all seven days on the home page. SC1, R8 3. On a phone, they select the number and ring it. SC1, R8 4. They come to the bakery, outside the website.

meaning.goes wrong: The orders cannot be fetched: Orders says so, and to reload the page. SC5, R9 A mark cannot be saved: the order stays under To do and says That did not save. Try again. SC5, R10
meaning.name: Handle an order
meaning.purpose: A member of staff sees the orders and marks each one ready.
meaning.steps: 1. A member of staff selects Staff in the footer, and enters the staff password. SC5, R11 2. They see the orders under To do and Ready, the soonest pick-up day first; a reload shows any placed since. SC5, R9 3. They make the cake, outside the website. 4. They select Mark ready, and the order moves to Ready. SC5, R10

meaning.name: Bakery details

meaning.details: The list comes with the page, and is changed by whoever looks after the website.
meaning.name: See what we bake
meaning.statement: The website shall show what the bakery bakes, each thing with its name, a picture and its price.

meaning.says: Given the eight things the bakery bakes, three of them cakes, when a customer opens What we bake, then all eight show, each with its name, picture and price.
Given Victoria sponge is a cake and Sourdough loaf is not, when a customer reads the list, then Victoria sponge offers Order this cake and Sourdough loaf offers no way to order it.

meaning.name: Mark an order ready
meaning.statement: When a member of staff marks an order ready, the website shall show it as ready.

meaning.says: Given an order under To do, when staff select Mark ready, then it moves to Ready.
Given two members of staff with the same order open, when the second selects Mark ready after the first, then it stays ready and nothing fails.
Given the mark cannot be saved, when staff select Mark ready, then the order stays under To do and says That did not save. Try again.

meaning.details: One password shared by the staff; a sign-in lasts until the browser is closed.
meaning.name: Only staff see the orders
meaning.statement: If someone who is not signed in as staff opens the orders, then the website shall ask for the staff password and show no order.

meaning.says: Given someone not signed in, when they open the orders' address, then the staff password is asked for and no order shows.
Given the right staff password, when it is sent, then the orders show.
Given a wrong staff password, when it is sent, then That password is not right shows and no order shows.

meaning.details: The words on the cake, up to 30 characters, and any allergies are optional. The customer pays at pick-up, so the website takes no payment, and needs no account.
meaning.name: Order a cake for pick-up
meaning.statement: When a customer sends an order with a cake, a size, a pick-up day, their name and their phone number, the website shall record it for pick-up at the bakery.

meaning.says: Given Victoria sponge, large, a pick-up day, Rosa Bell and 07700 900142, when she selects Place order, then an order is recorded with those details.
Given an order just sent, when the customer selects Place order a second time, then one order is recorded.
Given the words and allergies are left empty, when the order is sent, then it is recorded without them.
Given Victoria sponge on What we bake, when a customer chooses Order this cake, then the order form opens with Victoria sponge chosen.
Given the form is opened from the menu, when it shows, then no cake is chosen and the list of cakes offers only the three cakes.
Given the order cannot be recorded, when the customer selects Place order, then We could not place your order shows above the button with the bakery's phone number, and what they entered stays.

meaning.name: Say what needs fixing
meaning.statement: If a customer sends an order with a detail missing or not accepted, then the website shall keep what they entered and say beside each such detail what to fix.

meaning.says: Given no name is entered, when the customer selects Place order, then Please tell us your name shows under the name and everything entered stays.
Given the phone number is abc, when the customer selects Place order, then Please enter a phone number we can ring shows under the phone number.
Given three details need fixing, when the customer selects Place order, then Please check the 3 details below shows above the form and each says what to fix.
Given words of 31 characters, when the customer selects Place order, then Please keep the words to 30 characters shows under the words; 30 characters are accepted.

meaning.details: The bakery is closed on Mondays.
meaning.name: Pick-up days the bakery can do
meaning.statement: The website shall accept a pick-up day only if the bakery is open on it and it is at least two days after the order is placed.

meaning.says: Given an order placed on a Thursday, when Saturday is chosen as the pick-up day, then it is accepted.
Given an order placed on a Thursday, when Friday is chosen as the pick-up day, then We need two days' notice. Please choose a later day shows under the day.
Given a Monday, when it is chosen as the pick-up day, then We are closed on Mondays. Please choose another day shows under the day.

meaning.name: Say the order is placed
meaning.statement: When an order is recorded, the website shall show the customer its order number, the cake and its size, the pick-up day, the price to pay and where to collect it.

meaning.says: Given a large Victoria sponge is recorded, when Order placed shows, then it holds the order number, the cake and size, the pick-up day, 38 euros to pay at pick-up and 12 Mill Lane, Little Harbury.
Given Order placed is open, when the customer reloads it, then the same order shows and no second order is recorded.
Given no order has just been placed, when Order placed is opened, then the order form shows.
Given Order placed is open, when the customer reads it, then it says to ring 01632 960123, quoting the order number, to change or cancel the order.

meaning.name: Show the hours and address
meaning.statement: The website shall show the bakery's opening hours and address on every screen customers see.

meaning.says: Given any screen a customer sees, when they read its foot, then it shows the opening hours, 12 Mill Lane, Little Harbury and 01632 960123.
Given the home page, when a customer reads Find us, then it shows all seven days: Monday Closed, Tuesday to Friday 7:30 to 17:30, Saturday 8:00 to 15:00 and Sunday 9:00 to 13:00.
Given a customer on a phone, when they select the phone number, then their phone offers to ring it.

meaning.name: See the orders
meaning.statement: While a member of staff is signed in, the website shall show them the orders, the soonest pick-up day first.

meaning.says: Given orders for today, tomorrow and Saturday, when staff open the orders, then they show in that order, each with its number, pick-up day, cake, size, words, allergies, customer's name and phone number.
Given one order to do and one ready, when staff open the orders, then each shows under its own heading, To do or Ready.
Given no orders, when staff open the orders, then it says No orders yet.
Given an order placed while the list is open, when staff reload the page, then it shows under To do.
Given the orders cannot be fetched, when staff open them, then it says We could not load the orders, and to reload the page.
Given an order whose pick-up day has passed, when staff open the orders, then it no longer shows, collected or not.

meaning.who: Anyone who comes to the website to see what the bakery bakes, order a cake, or find its hours and address. They have no account.

meaning.name: staff
meaning.who: The people who work at the bakery, who see the orders and mark them ready.

meaning.name: speed
meaning.says: none: the owner set no target, and a site of five screens for about 20 orders a week has no step to hold to a number.

meaning.name: capacity
meaning.says: none: about 20 cake orders a week by the owner's count, with no growth to build for.

meaning.name: availability
meaning.says: none: no promise is made; if the website is down, customers ring 01632 960123, as they do today.

meaning.name: security
meaning.says: Only staff with the one shared password see orders. Nothing else on the website is private.

meaning.name: privacy
meaning.says: An order holds a customer's name, phone number and any allergies, only to make and hand over the cake, and is deleted the day after its pick-up day.

meaning.name: accessibility
meaning.says: Text contrast of at least 4.5:1, a visible keyboard focus on everything that can be used, and every screen usable by keyboard alone. The Accessibility foundation holds it.

meaning.name: devices
meaning.says: Phone first, desktop too, in current browsers.

meaning.name: languages
meaning.says: none: English only, prices in euros, one time zone: the bakery's.

meaning.name: proof
meaning.says: none: nothing needs showing afterwards, and an order is deleted the day after its pick-up day.

meaning.assumptions: Customers who ring today will order on the website instead. Check: ask the next ten phone customers to order on the website, and count how many do. Whoever looks after the website can change the list, the hours and the address when the owner asks. Check: name that person before building starts. Building and hosting the website costs less than it is worth to the bakery. Check: get a price before building starts. Almost every cake ordered is collected, since customers pay at pick-up. Check: count the cakes not collected in the first month. Keeping a customer's allergies until the day after pick-up needs no more care than this. Check: ask someone qualified before going live.
meaning.journey: 1. A customer rings the bakery to order a cake. 2. Someone takes the order by phone, usually while serving at the counter. This is the step that goes wrong: that is when mistakes happen. 3. Separately, someone rings just to ask when the bakery is open and where it is, and someone has to answer.
meaning.name: Mill Lane Bakery
meaning.non-goals: - Delivery: a cake is ordered for pick-up at the bakery, so nothing is sent out (D2). - Ordering anything other than a cake: the owner asked for cakes to be ordered, and everything else the bakery bakes is shown, not ordered (D2). - Paying on the website: customers pay at pick-up. - Telling the customer the cake is ready: they come on the day they chose. - Changing or cancelling an order on the website: they ring the bakery.
meaning.problem: The bakery takes about 20 cake orders a week by phone, usually while the staff are serving at the counter, and that is when mistakes happen. People also ring just to ask when the bakery is open and where it is. This is the owner's own account: the 20 is their figure, and the calls have never been counted.
meaning.summary: A small website for Mill Lane Bakery, where customers see what the bakery bakes, order a cake for pick-up, and find its opening hours and address. The bakery's staff see the orders there and mark them ready. It is for moving at least 15 of the bakery's 20 or so cake orders a week off the phone, where mistakes happen, and for cutting by half the calls just asking when the bakery is open and where it is.
meaning.users: Customers: people who want to see what the bakery bakes, order a cake for pick-up, or find its opening hours and address (U1). Today they ring the bakery. Staff: the people who work at the bakery, who see the orders and mark them ready (U2). Today they take cake orders by phone, usually while serving at the counter.
